question.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}]$ and the quadratic curve ${x}^{T}\,Ax=5.$ Given that $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=10$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ find the principal axes of the curve.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is symmetric. 
The principal axes of the curve 

$$
{x}^{T}\,Ax=5
$$

are the vectors that give an orthonormal eigenvector basis for $A.$ Let's now find these eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 6 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-10I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{13},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-3)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 6 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-3)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{13},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\,$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
